items.summary: Sjoerd De Jong aims to combat game development "stagnation" he says has emerged from Epic and Unity market dominance.
items.body: In June, Sjoerd De Jong—an Unreal Engine modder and map creator turned full-time specialist at Epic Games— announced that he was leaving the company after 12 years as its "lead evangelist" for Unreal. In a cryptic departure message, he said the games industry was at a "pivotal point," and he's aiming to "work out how to adapt and excel" at addressing the changing needs of videogame development. We now have a clearer idea of De Jong's plans for navigating the games industry's future. In an interview with This Week in Videogames , De Jong revealed what he's tackling next: He's building a game engine of his own. De Jong's nascent game engine competitor is called the Immens Engine, and he's building it alongside a small team of co-founders that includes former Epic technical director Arjan Brussee. According to De Jong, he's intending for Immens to serve as an alternative to the dominance of Unreal and Unity, whose market influence he said has led to a "stagnation" in game development for which challengers like Godot have only just recently started to emerge. items.body: Myst was a massive success: Not only was it the best-selling PC videogame of all time for years, it helped usher in the CD-ROM era, opening the door to expansive new technologies and previously unseen levels of fidelity in gaming. In 1993, Myst was nothing short of a revelation. The fortunes of Myst, and developer Cyan Worlds, have waned since then. The most recent game in the series, Myst 5: End of Ages, came out in 2005 and was reasonably well received but not a big seller; Cyan, after years of financial struggles, has moved onto Myst-like games including Firmament and Obduction, both of them reliant on crowdfunding. The studio laid off "roughly half" its staff in 2025, leading PC Gamer's Justin Wagner to write that "it's galling to see a historic indie like Cyan Worlds hit so hard" by the brutal, ongoing contraction of the game industry. Justin sure wasn't wrong about that, but some folks are finding this even more galling: Over the weekend Cyan released a teaser for a new Myst game, codenamed Project Anglerfish, which looks really good—and then said it's not in development because apparently publishers aren't interested. items.body: دعم جديد للنادي الإنجليزي يقترب ليدز يونايتد من التعاقد مع حارس مانشستر سيتي جيمس ترافورد، لتدعيم مركز حراسة المرمى في الفريق قبل انطلاق الموسم المقبل. ووفقًا لصحيفة " ذا أثليتيك " ، فإن ليدز يونايتد على وشك إتمام صفقة ضم حارس مرمى مانشستر سيتي مقابل حوالي 47 مليون يورو، شاملة المكافآت. ومن المتوقع أن يصبح الحارس الدولي الإنجليزي البالغ من العمر 23 عامًا، والذي كان يفضل الانتقال إلى ملعب إيلاند رود، ثالث صفقات النادي الصيفية بعد طارق محرموفيتش وهاري ويلسون. كان ليدز يونايتد حريصًا على تعزيز مركز حراسة المرمى بعد رحيل كارل دارلو إلى مانشستر يونايتد. وبعد أن أبدى نيوكاسل اهتمامًا بالحارس الإنجليزي لفترة، من المتوقع الآن أن ينضم ترافورد إلى ليدز. انضم ترافورد إلى مانشستر سيتي الصيف الماضي طامحًا إلى أن يصبح الحارس الأساسي، لكنه تراجع في الترتيب بعد وصول جيانلويجي دوناروما المفاجئ. في الموسم الماضي، شارك ترافورد في 17 مباراة في جميع المسابقات، وكان من أبرز مشاركاته في فوز السيتي بكأس الاتحاد الإنجليزي وكأس الرابطة.

items.title: حسمت.. نجم إنجلترا ينتقل إلى إنتر ميلان
items.summary: صفقة مجانية
items.body: صفقة مجانية حسم أحد نجوم مانشستر سيتي في الموسم المنصرم انتقاله إلى صفوف إنتر ميلان خلال الميركاتو الصيفي الجاري. وانتهى عقد جون ستونز مع مانشستر سيتي في 30 يونيو الماضي، وبات اللاعب مؤهلا للتوقيع مع أي نادٍ مجانا. وكتب فابريزيو رومانو، خبير الميركاتو، على حسابه بشبكة "إكس": "سينتقل جون ستونز إلى إنتر.. حسمت الصفقة بعدما تمت الموافقة على شروط العقد، وبات كل شيء مؤكدا". وأضاف: "يمتد عقد جون ستونز مع إنتر حتى يونيو 2028، دون وجود خيار التمديد لعام آخر، بينما سيكون الراتب حوالي 4 ملايين يورو صافية في الموسم". وتابع: "سيجري ستونز الفحوصات الطبية في مدينة ميلانو قريبًا". يذكر أن  ستونز سيجتمع بذلك مع زميله السابق في مانشستر سيتي، المدافع مانويل أكانجي، الذي انتقل إلى إنتر بشكل نهائي بعد انتهاء فترة إعارته التي استمرت لموسم 2025-2026. وكان بطل الدوري الإيطالي قد تعاقد هذا الصيف أيضا مع لاعب الوسط الدولي الصربي ألكسندر ستانكوفيتش قادما من كلوب بروج، والحارس إيفان بروفيديل قادما من لاتسيو. 🚨⚫️🔵 BREAKING: John Stones to Inter, here we go! items.title: Framework 13 Pro review
items.summary: The best laptop Framework's ever produced, and one of the best I've ever used.
items.body: The moment you touch the new Framework 13 Pro laptop you know it's different to what's come before. Despite the bubblegum pink USB Type-C ports I've jammed in either side of the machine, this is a serious laptop for serious work. But it's also still instantly recognisable as one of the company's eminently upgradeable and repairable notebooks. This is the true beauty of Framework's new machine, a laptop that at once exists as the pinnacle of its hardware journey, but also steadfastly refuses to compromise on the core principles that has made it one of my favourite PC builders. Though, it must be said, that refusal to compromise here comes at a hell of a cost because of the focus on ultra expensive LPCAMM2 memory. This is a next-generation Framework laptop, but is still completely compatible with every Framework 13 device the company has shipped in the past five years or so. That is a hell of an achievement, meaning that you could have an ageing 13-inch laptop and pick and choose from the company's Marketplace store whichever parts of the new machine you wanted. items.summary: Jesus Christ.
items.body: On January 20, 2019, Pope Francis delivered his weekly Angelus to St Peter's Square from a window in the Vatican's Apostolic Palace. In it, he enjoined the faithful to join him on the Church's then-new Click To Pray app—helpfully modelled by a nearby priest, wielding a tablet. Hundreds of thousands of people signed up in the years that followed. But maybe they shouldn't have, because it turns out the Click To Pray app was, until very recently, absolutely rife with info-leaking security holes. White-hat hacker BobDaHacker revealed in a July 24 blog post (via The Register ) that "The Pope's official app exposes 700,000+ user emails." The vulnerability has since been fixed, but it seems only after BobDaHacker went public with their investigation—inquiries made by the hacker and by journalists stretching back to January this year went unanswered. The vulnerability itself was pretty simple. When you sign up for Click To Pray, the site hands your user account an ID number. The first guy to sign up was one, the next was two, and so on, all the way into the hundreds of thousands. items.title: Micron's low power DRAM 'consumes approximately one-third the power of DDR5' in AI data center workloads, but I'm not sure that's good news
items.summary: Micron finds LPDDR5X can account for less than 7% of total system power.
items.body: AI's hunger for both power and memory, plus the resulting supply crisis of the latter, has led to many industry players engaging in a spot of creative problem solving. Case in point, Micron and Meta have collaborated on an experimental data centre roll out of low power DRAM. Micron has developed SOCAMM2 , a fresh form factor for LPDDR5X that is a "modular, serviceable module designed for servers." Testing used "Meta’s open-source DCPerf benchmark suite, which reflects production environments across a hyperscale fleet," and found that this low-power DRAM module "consumes approximately one-third the power of DDR5." According to Micron's white paper report , that accounts for under 7% of total system power. The white paper goes on to elaborate that LPDDR5X's "reduced operating voltage and advanced signalling allows bandwidth to scale without a corresponding rise in power consumption, resulting in better bandwidth-per-watt performance than conventional server memory." Basically, data centres can install more low power DRAM without also hiking up power-related operating costs. He argues, alongside companies like Google, OpenAI, and Meta, that the US should not aim to restrict open models 'prematurely', as they're important for the growth of AI (among other things). Taking a quick step back, Open models are ones that give access to weights or even code to see how it runs and to allow users to modify them. These can be run locally and are customisable. Closed models are those that tend to be run by specific companies, accessed via the cloud and APIs, and keep all their weights hidden. Open models out of China, like DeepSeek, became a problem for American AI firms at the start of last year. They exploded onto the scene, offering similar services to the likes of OpenAI, but totally free and available locally. Just last week, the Trump administration was reportedly looking to ban Chinese AI models due to cybersecurity concerns. According to Kawata, Capcom would like Resident Evil to be a fully annual franchise, but "producing a new entry in the Resident Evil series every year would be quite an undertaking and a difficult task." That's where the remakes come in. "Being able to revisit older games and remake them helps Capcom meet that goal of releasing a Resident Evil title each year, but it also allows the team to continually challenge themselves and hone their craft," said Kawata. items.body: First reported by Tom's Hardware , it's come to light that, not only are the four " Backward Compatibility on PC " original Xbox games released last week running on a double layer of Xbox console emulation, but savvy independent developers have already used those emulators to run other Xbox games on PC. It’s a damn crime that no game ripped off Red Faction: Guerrilla’s Geo-mod destruction feature. You take a hammer and you use it to smash out a panel of a wall and break through a pillar. Smash out a few more walls and maybe the building creaks. A few more whacks of the hammer later and the whole thing comes down, perhaps with you inside. And hey, maybe it knocks through another building on the way down. It’s still amazing to watch. Guerrilla does this one thing really well. items.title: Rockstar co-founder says 'I don't know if I personally care' if games release on disc, adds 'I love physical media'
items.summary: "If people want that, I think companies should provide it."
items.body: I still remember the long ritual of installing World of Warcraft to my parents' laptop as a young'un, mystified by the sheer number of discs it took to squeeze the game onto a hard drive. The more discs a game took to install, the better it must be, I figured—child me would be aghast at the contemporary world, where game boxes come with mere codes inside and PlayStation is killing off disc production . That last factoid has triggered commentary all over the industry and beyond, with everyone from Ubisoft's Yves Guillemot and French politician Jean-Luc Mélenchon weighing in. Speaking to IGN , Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser gave his own commentary on the physical vs. digital debate with a multifaceted answer. "I don't know that I care. For years, players have complained about the effects of skill-based matchmaking (SBMM), which is intended to level the playing field by sorting players into groups of similar skill. But some players claim that SBMM can outright flatten the experience, neutering much of the fun and unpredictability of arena shooting. Until recently, Activision had tried to convince players of the merits of SBMM. But last year saw a change in attitude from the publisher. And while I enjoy that part of the job, the journey itself is a dispiriting chore. Rail travel in the United Kingdom is a chaos of delays, overcrowding and overpriced sandwiches. Yet when I saw Great Western Express on Steam—an expansion for Train Sim World that recreates part of that route—I felt compelled to play it. Videogames are a powerful form of escapism for me, but what if I played one to achieve the complete opposite of that? Train Sim World is primarily a game about driving trains, but it's unique in that it also lets you be a passenger. Bath isn't in the game yet, so I start my journey at Reading, and I'm immediately struck by how well they've recreated the station. I've spent many hours here over the years waiting for delayed connections, and the layout is perfect—although the lack of a pasty shop is jarring. items.title: A classic Giger-inspired adventure game just got a sequel
items.summary: Tormentum 2 is out now.
items.body: H. R. Giger's biomechanical nightmares have inspired plenty of videogames. If we go way back, his work was repurposed for baffling puzzle adventure Dark Seed , and more recently there was the fleshy horror of Scorn . Tormentum: Dark Sorrow was more in the vein of the former than the latter, a point-and-click adventure that took Giger's stylings (and those of Zdzisław Beksiński too) as inspiration for its hand-painted horrors. A full 11 years after its release, and after eight years of development, Tormentum finally has a sequel. Tormentum 2 is a standalone game though, just one in a similar style, which is to say that it's full of bones and alien faces and naked people who are embedded in walls. In Tormentum 2 you're trapped inside a simulated world that's got out of hand, the supposedly digital characters within suddenly out of control and talking about gods from distant places. You have to cross the islands that make up this world, solving puzzles as you go, and working your way toward one of multiple endings. items.body: Villains monologue at us so much in videogames it's become passe. Oh, you're so evil you took over the radio station and replaced the friendly voice that's been guiding me since the tutorial just so you can tell me about your evil plan? Yawn. Use that radio to sing a song at me, maybe then I'll pay attention. Sing during a boss fight and I'll pay even more attention. I'm not sure where this trend started, but the videogame boss who is so extra they can't help but perform an entire song-and-dance routine while kicking your ass has become a delightful trend—though not all the entries on this list are boss-fight songs. Okamoto spoke in a lecture at Japan's CEDEC 2026⁠—that's "CESA Developer's Conference" longwise, or "Computer Entertainment Supplier's Association Developer's Conference" extra longwise. In his talk, "The Art of Producing Silent Hill," Okamoto said that he believes being well-read is an important trait for videogame producers to cultivate, and that reading the entire body of work by any game writer he collaborated with was a matter of "basic respect." But that drive for literacy doesn't just stop with Okamoto. In the interest of having strong "input" for the developers, Okamoto said that, "within the team, we put pressure on each other, especially among the scenario writers, to read at least 100 to 200 books a year." items.title: Modders finally got a high-quality third-person camera working in Baldur's Gate 3 for all you Dragon Age sickos
items.summary: Up close and personal.
items.body: A CRPG in the vein of Baldur's Gate without a bird's-eye view camera sure sounds wrong, but it feels so right. If you're looking for something a little more Dragon Age and less Divinity for your next replay, Modder Relysia has gone and stuck an over-the-shoulder third-person camera in Baldur's Gate 3, uploading it to Nexus Mods last week, and it looks a lot better than you may expect. In the brief showcase teaser, you can see the player wandering around the Undercity Ruins. Animations are a tad jittery, but because BG3's environments are made to be zoomed in and gawked at and shown off in dialog cutscenes, everything is at a believable scale. I'm not sure this would work in all of the game's environments to the same extent, but that it works at all is nifty. You've always been able to get the camera up close in BG3, but it's always angled slightly downward, feeling less like a proper third person action game cam, and more like a compromise with its classico tactico overhead view. Even playing with a game pad, it's distinct from other videogame cameras.
